real: A 58cm metal sphere beeps into orbit and starts the Space Age
source: Sputnik 1, the first artificial Earth satellite, was launched by the Soviet Union on 4 October 1957 and became the object that kicked off the Space Age, prompting a US-Soviet space race that would last decades.

real: A human orbits the Earth for the first time in 108 minutes
source: Vostok 1, launched by the Soviet Union on 12 April 1961, carried cosmonaut Yuri Gagarin into orbit for 108 minutes, making him the first human in space and the first to orbit the Earth.

real: A moon mission is saved by duct tape and a box built from the spacecraft itself
source: Apollo 13, the 1970 mission intended to be the third Moon landing, suffered a catastrophic oxygen-tank explosion en route and brought its three crew members home safely in a dramatic rescue that became one of the most famous 'successful failures' in spaceflight history.

real: Two humans walk on the Moon while 600 million people watch on TV
source: Apollo 11, which landed on the Moon on 20 July 1969, carried astronauts Neil Armstrong and Buzz Aldrin to the lunar surface, making it the first crewed Moon landing and one of the most-watched events in television history.

real: An astronomer maps 'canals' across Mars and sparks a century of alien speculation
source: Astronomer Percival Lowell, who mapped an extensive network of 'canals' across the surface of Mars in the early 1900s, popularized the idea of intelligent life on the planet and shaped science-fiction and public speculation about aliens for over a century.

real: A physicist asks why, if the universe should teem with life, the sky is silent
source: The Fermi paradox, named after physicist Enrico Fermi, is the apparent contradiction between the high probability that intelligent extraterrestrial life exists somewhere in the vast universe and the complete lack of evidence for, or contact with, such civilizations.

real: A record of Earth's sounds, music and greetings is flung into interstellar space
source: The Voyager Golden Record, launched aboard the Voyager probes in 1977, is a gold-plated phonograph record containing sounds of Earth, music from many cultures, and greetings in 55 languages, now sailing through interstellar space as a message to any civilization that might find it.

real: A computer passes a 'test' that says machines can think — but only on paper
source: The Turing test, proposed by Alan Turing in 1950, is a standard for machine intelligence in which a machine passes if it can hold a conversation indistinguishable from a human, and it remains the most cited thought experiment in the field of artificial intelligence.

real: The first large electronic computer is the size of a room and weighs 30 tons
source: ENIAC, completed in 1945 at the University of Pennsylvania, was the first general-purpose, electronic, programmable digital computer, weighing about 30 tons and filling a room, and it is regarded as a foundational machine in the history of computing.

real: A mathematician writes the first 'program' — for a machine that was never built
source: Ada Lovelace, an English mathematician and writer, is widely regarded as the first computer programmer for the notes she wrote on Charles Babbage's Analytical Engine in the 1840s, which included what is considered the first published algorithm intended to be carried out by a machine that was never actually built.

real: A CERN physicist proposes a 'mesh' of hypertext documents — and gives it away for free
source: The World Wide Web, proposed by Tim Berners-Lee at CERN in 1989, was developed as a system of hypertext documents linked over the internet, and it was made freely available to all, becoming the foundation of the modern internet as most people use it today.

real: A gene-editing tool borrowed from bacteria can rewrite living DNA
source: CRISPR, a gene-editing technology derived from a natural bacterial defense system, was adapted in the early 2010s as a precise tool for modifying DNA and has since transformed biology and medicine, enabling scientists to edit genes in living organisms with unprecedented accuracy.

real: A 100-billion-dollar particle collider confirms the particle that gives mass to everything
source: The Higgs boson, a subatomic particle predicted by the Standard Model of particle physics, was confirmed by the CERN particle accelerator in 2012 after decades of searching, completing a central piece of the theory that explains how particles acquire mass.
